slice: Reject floating DIV operands before literal-zero handling

scope.runtime: One planner file moves the existing operand type lookups ahead of literal-zero handling and rejects floating inputs using DataType::is_floating and the existing PlanError::invalid constructor. Valid queries keep their previous lowering and execution.
scope.callers: Both SQL DIV operator syntax and div(a,b) resolve through spark_div. Other operators and functions are unchanged.
scope.benchmark: Ten source lines add three DIV query shapes and their full-value expectations to the existing subquery harness. Both measured binaries use this same source.

corpus.origin: Local 76-query type/placement/control matrix captured against Spark 4.2.0 before implementing the guard. Multirow controls use explicit ordering. Not an upstream CI list.

provenance.implementation_origin: Local planner guard matching Spark input-type rejection. The inspected Sail revision still has the permissive lowering; no additional Sail code or upstream fix was imported.
provenance.binary_builds: Both benchmark binaries were built here with identical expanded harness source. Before-probe and before-runner are the verified parent binaries; the parent artifact records their final import-order-only source cleanup. All after binaries were built from the recorded after sources.

limitations: Four new value/type or error-stage differences remain: INT_MIN DIV -1 in both ANSI modes, non-ANSI BIGINT_MIN DIV -1, and ANSI string/integer DIV. Integer widening, overflow policy and implicit string coercion are separate work.

Prior corpora retain four original, twenty ROUND, sixty-five floating division and twenty-four floating-zero value/type or error-stage differences, plus five previously recorded same-stage error-cause gaps. Counts include repeated query shapes and ANSI modes.

All 102 new floating observations and sixty prior floating DIV observations reject at planning. Of these, 158 expose the explicit floating-input error; four ORDER BY cases pass through the pre-existing generic sort-expression error wrapper. Eighteen new observations previously agreed at the coarse planning-error level but now expose the correct type cause.

Numeric comparison checks ordered numeric values, types and coarse error stage, not complete schema metadata or structured error conditions. Prior 188 focused error-cause/signed-zero checks are preserved. Delta comparison separately checks names, nullability and metadata.

Performance measurements cover the successful DIV expressions and controls shown, not all query shapes or rejection latency. The source adds no per-row work to accepted queries, but the measurements do not establish zero planning overhead.

CPU frequency is not fixed and the host is not isolated. Default-allocator ROUND time changes by +23.67% despite effectively identical instructions; fixed diagnostic thresholds give +0.46%. Both observations are retained, and production allocator settings are unchanged.
